title: ～さえ — even ～
summary: Takes an extreme or easy example to imply that everything else is naturally so: “even ～.” Used for something surprising or extreme, with a negative or an affirmative result. It replaces を, が or は, and stacks with other particles.

patterns.gloss: noun + さえ: even this (子どもさえ解ける)

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋ことさえ／動詞ます形＋さえ
patterns.gloss: even doing ～ (書くことさえ面倒だ)

body.p: 子どもさえ解ける means “even a child can solve it, so of course an adult can.” Conversely, 時間さえない means “I lack even the simplest thing, so the rest is all the more impossible.” It works in both affirmative and negative sentences.

body.h: Compared with も and まで
body.p: も simply means “also,” while さえ points to an extreme example. For verbs use 〜ことさえ, as in 名前を書くことさえ面倒だ. The form でさえ (子どもでさえ) is also common. すら has the same function with more emphasis.

examples.ja: その問題（もんだい）は子（こ）どもさえ解（と）ける。
examples.romaji: Sono mondai wa kodomo sae tokeru.
examples.tr: Even a child can solve that problem.
examples.note: An easy example implies adults can too.

examples.ja: 忙（いそが）しくて、昼（ひる）ごはんを食（た）べる時間（じかん）さえない。
examples.romaji: Isogashikute, hirugohan o taberu jikan sae nai.
examples.tr: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat lunch.

examples.ja: 疲（つか）れすぎて、名前（なまえ）を書（か）くことさえ面倒（めんどう）だ。
examples.romaji: Tsukaresugite, namae o kaku koto sae mendō da.
examples.tr: I'm so tired that even writing my name feels like a bother.
examples.note: Verb dictionary form + ことさえ.

pitfalls: Do not attach it directly to a verb: × 書くさえ, ○ 書くことさえ.
さえ〜ば (〜さえすれば) is a separate use meaning “if only.”
